==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈslɪp/|[ˈslɪp]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-slip.ogg|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|en-au-slip.ogg|a=AU}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪp|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|slip}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=slide|:inh|enm:slippen>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|slippen}}, probably from {{der|en|gml|slippen}}, from {{der|en|osx|*slippian}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*slippjan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*slipjaną|t=to glide}}, an iterative form of {{m|gem-pro|*slīpaną|t=to slip, slide}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sleyb-|t=slimy; to slide}}. Possibly ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*slewbʰ-|t=slip, slide}}, or related to {{der|en|gem-pro|*slībaną|t=to split}}; related to {{cog|ang|slipor|t=slippery}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|slipje|t=to slip}}, {{cog|nl|slippen|t=to slip}}, {{cog|nds-de|slippen}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|+,~t}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To lose one’s traction on a slippery surface; to [[slide]] due to a lack of [[friction]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1960|month=March|title=Motive Power Miscellany: Western Region|journal=Trains Illustrated|page=184|text=[...] but in the damp conditions prevailing the driver sensibly was unwilling to attempt the climb up through Combe Down tunnel without help, for fear of '''slipping''' to a standstill in the unventilated bore, {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=May 9, 2012|author=Jonathan Wilson|title=Europa League: Radamel Falcao’s Atlético Madrid rout Athletic Bilbao|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/2012/may/09/atletico-madrid-athletic-bilbao-europa-league|passage=Fernando Amorebieta seemed to have checked him, but a stepover created a fraction of room that became significant as the defender '''slipped''', giving Falcao just enough space to curl a superb finish into the top corner.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011065933/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/may/09/atletico-madrid-athletic-bilbao-europa-league|archivedate=11 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[err]]. #* {{RQ:King James Version|Ecclesiasticus|19|16|passage=There is one that '''slippeth''' in his speach, but not from his heart, and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To accidentally reveal a [[secret]] or otherwise say something unintentionally. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move or fly (out of place); to shoot; often with ''out'', ''off'', ''etc.'' #: {{ux|en|A bone may '''slip''' out of place.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[elude]] or [[evade]] by smooth movement. #: {{ux|en|I caught the thief, but he '''slipped''' my grasp and ran away.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[pass]] (a note, money, ''etc.''), often [[covertly]]. #: {{ux|en|She thanked the porter and '''slipped''' a ten-dollar bill into his hand.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause to move smoothly and quickly; to slide; to convey gently or secretly. #* {{RQ:Arbuthnot Law|year=1733|chapter=XI|chaptername=The Apprehending, Examination, and Imprisonment of Jack, for Suspicion of Poisoning|page=119|passage=Tvvo other VVitneſſes gave the follovving Evidence; That in his officious Attendance upon his Miſtreſs, he had try'd to '''ſlip''' a Povvder into her Drink, and that he vvas once catch'd endeavouring to ſtifle her vvith a Pillovv as ſhe vvas aſleep; {{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1913|author={{w|Edgar Rice Burroughs}}|title={{w|The Return of Tarzan}}|publisher=Ballantine Books|location=New York|year_published=1963|page=43|passage=“This is a very urgent message for the countess’ ears alone,” replied Rokoff. “Tell her that she must arise and '''slip''' something about her and come to the telephone. I shall call up again in five minutes.”}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move [[quickly]] and often [[secretively]]; to depart, withdraw, enter, appear, intrude, or escape as if by sliding. #: {{syn|en|slink}} #: {{ux|en|Some errors '''slipped''' into the appendix.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|Aeneis|text=Thrice the flitting shadow '''slipped''' away.}} #* {{RQ:Prior Alma|canto=II|passage=Thus one tradesman '''slips''' away, / To give his partner fairer play.}} #* {{RQ:Stevenson Treasure Island|text=We '''slipped''' along the hedges, noiseless and swift {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|figuratively}} To move [[down]]; to [[slide]]. #: {{ux|en|Profits have '''slipped''' over the past six months.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|hunting|falconry}} To release (a dog, a [[bird of prey]], ''etc.'') to go after a [[quarry]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|act=V|scene=ii|passage=Lucento '''slipped''' me like his greyhound.}} #* {{RQ:Asbjornsen Braekstad Tales|page=78|passage='Well, it was one morning early in the spring,' said Lars, 'that I started for Linderudsœter, where I '''slipped''' Rap, and he was soon in full cry and made the hillside ring.'}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|aviation|of an aircraft}} {{clipping of|en|sideslip||to fly with the longitudinal axis misaligned with the relative wind}}. # {{lb|en|transitive|cooking}} To remove the [[skin]] of a soft fruit, such as a [[tomato]] or [[peach]], by [[blanching]] briefly in boiling water, then transferring to cold water so that the skin peels, or slips, off easily. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To omit; to lose by negligence. #* {{RQ:Jonson Catiline|passage=And '''slip''' no advantage / That may secure you.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut slips from; to cut; to take off; to make a slip or slips of. #: {{ux|en|to '''slip''' a piece of cloth or paper}} #* {{RQ:Mortimer Husbandry|passage=The branches also may be '''slipped''' and planted.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause to slip or slide off, or out of place. #: {{ux|en|A horse '''slips''' his bridle; a dog '''slips''' his collar.}} # To bring forth (young) prematurely; to [[slink]]. # {{lb|en|transitive|business}} To cause (a schedule or release, ''etc.'') to go, or let it go, beyond the allotted deadline. =====Translations===== {{trans-top-see|to lose one's traction|slide}} *
